A country makes money mostly from taxes. These are payments that people and businesses make to the government. The government then spends the money on things like pensions and hospitals.
This year, the United States spent almost $2 trillion more than it collected. That is called a deficit. It is a very big number, and it is bigger than last year.
To pay for the gap, the government borrows. When you borrow, you pay back extra, called interest. The government's interest bill is now more than $1 trillion in one year.
The government also got less tax from companies this year. And some taxes on goods coming from other countries were stopped by a court. The United States has had a deficit for 25 years in a row.
levels.why: Borrowing and interest add up, so leaders have to think carefully about money.

levels.headline: America's pocket money ran out, so it borrowed
levels.body:
Imagine you get £10 pocket money each week, but you spend £12. To buy everything, you must borrow £2 from a friend. When you pay your friend back, you give a little extra as thanks. This is a bit like a deficit.
The United States is a big country, and the government spends a huge amount on things like pensions for older people and health care. This year it spent almost $2 trillion more than it collected in taxes. That is a big number.
It borrowed to fill the gap. Now it has to pay back extra each year, called interest. This extra costs more than $1 trillion. The country has done this for 25 years.
levels.why: If you spend more than you have, you must borrow, and borrowing has a cost.

levels.headline: Spending more than you get is called a deficit
levels.body:
Imagine your family gets paid every month. Some months, you spend more than you got. To manage, you borrow some money from the bank. Next month, you pay back what you borrowed, plus a little extra for the bank.
The US government does the same, but with huge numbers. This year it spent almost $2 trillion more than it received. The country has done that for 25 years in a row.
The extra it pays back, called interest, is now more than $1 trillion a year. That is a lot of money that cannot be used for other things.
Grown-ups are worried, because the more you borrow, the more you must pay back.
levels.why: It is wise to be careful with borrowed money, whether you are a family or a country.

headline: Government launches independent review of security for people in public life

terms.meaning: Measures, such as police protection and guidance, that keep people safe from threats.
An investigation led by someone outside government who reports on what should change.

levels.headline: Government launches independent review of security for people in public life
levels.body:
The Home Office announced on 12 October a root-and-branch review of protective security for people in public life. It will be led by Sir Stephen Lovegrove, a former national security adviser, and report within six months.
The review will look at the issue from every angle, including physical threats, online risks and the dangers posed within a more polarised society. It covers high-profile individuals including royals, ministers, MPs, locally elected representatives and other prominent figures in British politics. It will not assess individual cases.
As an interim measure, police support is being widened to people who are no longer MPs, such as former members of Parliament, peers and party spokespeople.
The government cited recent events as raising concern. The review will build on Sir Robert Buckland's separate inquiry into the killing of Sir David Amess, which is looking at MPs' security in their constituencies.
levels.why: Threats to people in public life are a risk to democracy as well as to the individuals themselves.

levels.headline: Former national security adviser to lead review of protection for public figures
levels.body:
The Home Office announced on 12 October an independent review of protective security for people in public life. Sir Stephen Lovegrove, a former national security adviser, will lead it and report within six months.
It will examine physical threats, online risks and the dangers in a more polarised society, and cover royals, ministers, MPs, local councillors and other prominent figures in British politics. It will not assess individual cases.
In the meantime, police support will be extended to people who are no longer MPs, including former MPs, peers and party spokespeople.
The review will build on Sir Robert Buckland's separate review following the killing of Sir David Amess, which examines MPs' security in their constituencies.
levels.why: The findings could change how politicians and public figures are protected.

levels.headline: Review to look at how people in public life are kept safe
levels.body:
The government announced on 12 October a review of the way people in public life are protected. Sir Stephen Lovegrove, who used to be the national security adviser, will lead it. He must report within six months.
The review will look at physical threats, dangers online, and the risks that come from a society in which people are more divided. It covers royals, ministers, MPs, local councillors and other well-known political figures. It will not look at individual cases.
For now, police protection is being offered to more people, including former MPs, peers and party spokespeople.
The work builds on a separate review by Sir Robert Buckland into the killing of Sir David Amess.
levels.why: Better protection helps people to take part in politics without fear.

levels.headline: Government orders review of security for politicians and other public figures
levels.body:
The Home Office said on 12 October that it is setting up a review of how people in public life are protected. Sir Stephen Lovegrove, a former national security adviser, will lead it and must report in six months.
The review will look at many kinds of risk. These include physical attacks, threats online and the dangers of a more divided society. It covers members of the royal family, ministers, MPs, local politicians and other well-known figures. It will not decide individual cases.
Meanwhile, police help is being widened to include people who are no longer MPs, such as former MPs, peers and party spokespeople.
It builds on another review by Sir Robert Buckland, about the killing of Sir David Amess.
levels.why: Protecting people who serve the public helps keep democracy working.

levels.headline: A review will look at keeping public figures safe
levels.body:
The government has asked for a review of how to keep people in public life safe. This includes politicians, members of the royal family, ministers and councillors. The announcement came on 12 October.
Sir Stephen Lovegrove will lead the work. He used to be the national security adviser. He has six months to report back.
He will look at dangers from people in person and online, and at the risks that come from society being more divided. He will not look at individual cases.
For now, the police will give help to more people. That includes former MPs, members of the House of Lords and spokespeople for political parties. The work also builds on an earlier review about the killing of MP Sir David Amess.
levels.why: If public figures are safe, they can do their jobs freely and people can have a say.

levels.headline: People in public life may get better protection
levels.body:
The government wants to make sure people in public life are safe. These are people such as MPs, ministers, local councillors and members of the royal family. On 12 October it announced a review of how they are protected.
Sir Stephen Lovegrove will lead it. He used to be the government's top adviser on national security. He has six months to finish.
He will study threats in person and threats online. He will also look at how a society where people strongly disagree can make things riskier. He will not look at individual cases.
For now, police help will be given to more people, such as former MPs and spokespeople for parties. This follows an earlier review about the killing of MP Sir David Amess.
levels.why: People in public life should be able to do their work without fear.

levels.headline: A review of how to keep politicians and other public figures safe
levels.body:
The government has said it will look at how to keep people in public life safe. This includes MPs, ministers, councillors and members of the royal family. People in public life are people who work in politics or are well known for serving the public.
The review was announced on 12 October. A man called Sir Stephen Lovegrove will lead it. He used to advise the government on national security. He has six months to report.
He will look at threats in person and online. He will not look at single cases.
For now, the police will protect more people, such as people who used to be MPs.
levels.why: Keeping people safe lets them do their jobs, and helps people trust democracy.

levels.headline: The government wants to keep important people safe
levels.body:
Some people have jobs that help run the country. They might be MPs, who speak for people in Parliament. Others are ministers, who lead government departments. Some are councillors, who work in local areas. They can all sometimes face threats.
On 12 October the government said it will look at how to keep these people safe. A man called Sir Stephen Lovegrove will lead the work. He used to give advice to the government about keeping the country safe. He has six months to finish.
He will look at dangers in person and dangers online. For now, the police will help more people, including people who used to be MPs.
levels.why: When people feel safe, they are more willing to do jobs that help the community.

levels.headline: Looking after the people who help run the country
levels.body:
Think of the person who is class monitor or leads the school council. They help the whole school. But sometimes other people can be unkind to them, just because they have to make choices.
In the same way, there are people who help run our country. They are MPs, ministers and councillors. Sometimes people are unkind or even dangerous towards them online or in person.
The government has asked a man called Sir Stephen Lovegrove to look at how to keep them safe. He has six months to find ideas.
For now, the police will help look after more people, even some who used to be MPs.
levels.why: Everyone should be able to do a job for their community without fear.

levels.headline: The government is looking at how to keep helpers safe
levels.body:
Some grown-ups have jobs where they help lots of people. They make choices for towns and for the country. Some are called MPs. Some are called ministers. Others are called councillors.
But sometimes people are unkind to them. A few people even try to scare or hurt them. That is not right.
The government has asked a person called Sir Stephen Lovegrove to find ways to keep them safe. He will look at what is happening in real life and online. He has six months to work on it.
For now, the police will help look after more people, even some who used to be MPs.
levels.why: People who help others should be safe while they work.
